links_touching_record.rationale: FB2-VER-EXE-000027 is the execution record for FB2-VER-TMS-000027. It carries execution_kind 'none' and outcome 'blocked' with the specific unblock condition that applies to that measure, so the link asserts that an execution record exists and honestly reports that nothing was run. It is not evidence that the measure passed.

FB2-REV-000017 reviewed FB2-VER-EXE-000027 at revision 1 and enumerates it in reviewed_ids with the sha256 of the artefact's content at review time. Direction follows the pre-existing reviewed_by links in this registry, which run review -> artefact. This link was authored together with the review it belongs to and its target digest was computed from the file on disk, so the two agree by construction rather than by later repair; the review has not been re-examined since.

shape_note: Deliberately not shaped like a corpus record: no top-level id, profile, artifact_type or source_refs, so that generating packets cannot change any coverage number. See the module docstring of make_review_packets.py.

signature_block._recording: Transcribe a completed signature into the record as human_approval_status plus a revision_history entry naming the reviewer, and archive the signed packet outside docs/artifacts/reviews/packets/.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record, and the corpus rule `human_approval_rejected` fails validation on any record whose human_approval_status is not pending, so no tool can manufacture the state.
